operations.description:
Retrieves a paginated list of products from the authenticated customer's wishlist.

This endpoint returns all active wishlist items owned by the current customer, displaying product information including the main image, product name, base price, and seller shop name. The wishlist helps customers track products they are interested in for future purchase.

The operation supports pagination to handle large numbers of saved items and ensures performance. Results can be sorted by when the product was added to the wishlist (created_at) or by product name. Optional date range filters allow customers to find products added within specific time periods.

Only the authenticated customer can access their own wishlist. The response excludes soft-deleted products and soft-deleted wishlist entries. Stock availability status is not included in wishlist responses - customers must navigate to individual product pages to check current inventory levels.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_wishlist_items table filtered by authenticated customer's member ID. Join with shopping_mall_products to retrieve product details (name, base_price, main image). Join with shopping_mall_sellers through product to get seller shop name. Apply pagination using cursor-based or offset pagination on created_at timestamp. Support sorting by created_at (ascending/descending) and product name. Filter by optional date range (created_at from/to). Exclude soft-deleted wishlist items (deleted_at IS NULL) and soft-deleted products. Return IPageIShoppingMallWishlistItem.ISummary with wishlist items containing product summary information. Do NOT include stock availability status in response per business rules.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of wishlist item summary records containing product information optimized for customer wishlist display.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for filtering and paginating wishlist items including pagination parameters, sorting options, and optional date range filters for when products were added to the wishlist.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific wishlist item by its unique identifier.

This operation returns detailed information about a single product in the customer's wishlist, including the product's main image, name, base price, and seller shop name. The wishlist item includes the timestamp when the product was added to help customers track their product interest over time.

The operation enforces strict ownership validation: customers can only access wishlist items that belong to their own account. Attempts to access another customer's wishlist item are rejected with an access violation error.

If the wishlist item has been soft-deleted (either because the customer removed it or the product was deleted by the seller), the operation returns a not found error. This ensures customers only see active wishlist entries.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the shopping_mall_wishlist_items table by the provided wishlistItemId UUID.

Join with shopping_mall_products to retrieve product details including name, base price, and main image URL.
Join with shopping_mall_sellers through the product to get the seller's shop name.

Validate ownership: verify that the shopping_mall_member_id matches the authenticated customer's ID. Reject with 403 if mismatch.

Check deleted_at is null. If deleted_at is set, return 404 not found.

Return the complete wishlist item with embedded product information including product id, name, main image URL, base price, and seller shop name.

Handle edge cases: wishlist item not found (404), product was deleted (404), access violation (403).

responseBody.description: Complete wishlist item details including the product information and the timestamp when the product was added to the wishlist.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the wishlist item to retrieve (UUID format).
parameters.name: wishlistItemId

prerequisites.description: Product must exist before it can be added to a customer's wishlist
Wishlist item must be created before it can be retrieved

operations.description:
Add a product to the authenticated customer's wishlist for future purchase consideration.

This operation creates a new wishlist entry linking the customer to a product they want to track. The wishlist operates at the product level, not at the variant level, so customers save entire products rather than specific variants. Each product can appear only once in a customer's wishlist.

The system automatically records the timestamp when the product is added. If the customer attempts to add a product that is already in their wishlist, the request is rejected with a duplicate entry error. When a product is deleted by its seller, all associated wishlist entries are automatically soft-deleted to maintain data integrity.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new wishlist item for the authenticated customer.

1. Extract memberId from authenticated session context (not from request body)
2. Validate productId exists in shopping_mall_products table
3. Check unique constraint: verify no existing active wishlist item with same [memberId, productId] combination
4. Insert new record into shopping_mall_wishlist_items with:
   - id: generated UUID
   - shopping_mall_member_id: from session
   - shopping_mall_product_id: from request body
   - created_at: current timestamp
   - updated_at: current timestamp
   - deleted_at: null
5. Return the created wishlist item with full entity data
6. Handle duplicate violation: return 409 conflict if product already in wishlist
7. Handle product not found: return 404 if productId doesn't exist

responseBody.description: The newly created wishlist item containing the product reference and creation timestamp.

requestBody.description: Product identifier to add to the customer's wishlist. The member ID is automatically derived from the authenticated session context.

prerequisites.description: Product must exist in the catalog before it can be added to a customer's wishlist

operations.description:
Remove a product from the customer's wishlist.

This operation deletes a specific wishlist item, removing the product from the customer's saved products list. Customers use this to curate their wishlist by removing items they have purchased or are no longer interested in tracking for future purchase.

The wishlist item is soft-deleted by setting the deleted_at timestamp. The customer can only delete their own wishlist items. Attempting to delete another customer's wishlist item will be rejected.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Delete the wishlist item by setting deleted_at timestamp to current time.

1. Verify the wishlist item exists and belongs to the authenticated customer
2. Check that deleted_at is currently null (item not already deleted)
3. Update the record by setting deleted_at to current timestamp
4. Return success response

Reject with 404 if wishlist item does not exist or does not belong to the customer. Reject with 400 if item is already deleted.

parameters.description: UUID of the wishlist item to remove (scoped to the authenticated customer).
parameters.name: wishlistItemId

operations.description:
Retrieve the authenticated customer's shopping cart with all cart items.

Returns the customer's personal shopping cart containing all items they have added for potential purchase. Each cart item includes the product variant details, quantity, and pricing information. The cart belongs exclusively to the authenticated customer and cannot be accessed by other users.

The response includes the cart metadata (creation and update timestamps) and all cart items with their associated product variant information. Cart total price is calculated dynamically from the cart items and is not stored in the database.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_carts table filtering by authenticated member's ID. Join with shopping_mall_cart_items to retrieve all items in the cart. Join with shopping_mall_product_variants to get variant details including option values. Join with shopping_mall_products to get product names and descriptions. Return the cart entity with nested items array. If cart doesn't exist, return null or create empty cart. Handle soft-deleted carts appropriately.

responseBody.description: Complete cart entity with all cart items including product variant details, quantities, and pricing information for the authenticated customer's shopping cart.

operations.description:
Add a product variant to the customer's shopping cart.

This endpoint allows customers to add items to their shopping cart by specifying a product variant and quantity. If the same variant already exists in the cart, the quantity is combined with the existing amount rather than creating a duplicate entry, enforced by the unique constraint on cart and product variant.

The cart is automatically determined from the authenticated customer's session, as each customer has exactly one active cart. The operation returns the created or updated cart item with the final quantity.

Customers can add available product variants to their cart for later purchase during checkout. Unavailable variants may be added but will block checkout until removed.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create or update a cart item for the authenticated customer's cart.

1. Retrieve the authenticated customer's cart from session (shopping_mall_carts where member_id = current user and deleted_at IS NULL)
2. Check if cart item already exists for the given product variant (unique constraint on shopping_mall_cart_id, shopping_mall_product_variant_id)
3. If exists: UPDATE the quantity by adding the new quantity to existing quantity
4. If not exists: INSERT new cart item with the specified quantity
5. Return the cart item with final quantity
6. Validate product variant exists and is active before adding
7. Validate quantity is positive integer (minimum 1)

Edge cases:
- If variant is out of stock, still allow adding but mark as unavailable in cart view
- If quantity exceeds available stock, allow adding but checkout will be blocked
- Cart is created automatically if customer doesn't have one yet

responseBody.description: The created or updated cart item with the final quantity after combining with existing items.

requestBody.description: Product variant identifier and quantity to add to the cart. Quantity must be a positive integer. If the variant already exists in the cart, the quantity will be combined with the existing amount.

prerequisites.description: Product variant must be created by a seller before customers can add it to their shopping cart. The variant must exist with a valid ID, SKU code, and option values.

operations.description:
Update the quantity of a specific cart item.

This endpoint allows customers to modify the quantity of a product variant in their shopping cart. The cart item must exist and belong to the authenticated customer. Quantity can be increased or decreased based on product availability.

The operation validates that the requested quantity is positive and does not exceed available stock. If the quantity is set to zero or below, the item should be removed from the cart instead.
operations.name: update
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_cart_items by cartItemId UUID. Verify the cart item exists and belongs to the authenticated customer through the cart's member_id relationship. Validate the new quantity is a positive integer. Check product variant availability and stock levels. Update the quantity field and updated_at timestamp. Return the complete updated cart item with product variant details joined if needed for response.

responseBody.description: The updated cart item with the new quantity and current timestamps.

parameters.description: Cart item UUID (global scope)
parameters.name: cartItemId

requestBody.description: Update request containing the new quantity for the cart item.

prerequisites.description: Cart item must be created before it can be updated. The cart item is identified by cartItemId in the path parameter and must exist in the system.

operations.description:
Remove a specific item from the customer's shopping cart.

This operation permanently deletes the specified cart item from the customer's cart. The removal is immediate and cannot be undone. After deletion, the cart total price is automatically recalculated to reflect the removed item.

Customers can remove any item from their cart at any time before order placement, including both available and unavailable items. This operation is commonly used when customers decide they no longer want to purchase a specific item or need to remove unavailable items before checkout.

The cart item is identified by its unique cartItemId. Only the cart owner (authenticated customer) can delete items from their own cart. Attempting to delete another customer's cart item will result in an authorization error.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Delete the cart item record from shopping_mall_cart_items table by cartItemId.

1. Verify the cart item exists and belongs to the authenticated customer
2. Delete the cart item record from shopping_mall_cart_items table
3. Recalculate the parent cart's total price by summing remaining cart items
4. Return success response (204 No Content or null response body)

Business rules:
- Customer can only delete items from their own cart
- Deletion is immediate and permanent (not reversible)
- Cart total must be recalculated after deletion
- Works for both available and unavailable items
- If cart becomes empty, cart remains but with zero items

Edge cases:
- Cart item already deleted: return 404 Not Found
- Cart item belongs to different customer: return 403 Forbidden
- Cart item does not exist: return 404 Not Found

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the cart item to remove (UUID format, scoped to customer's cart)
parameters.name: cartItemId

prerequisites.description: Cart item must be created before it can be deleted. This operation creates the cart item record in shopping_mall_cart_items that the DELETE operation will remove.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of customer orders with filtering and sorting capabilities.

This endpoint allows customers to browse their order history with flexible search criteria. Orders are sorted by creation date (newest first) by default. Customers can filter orders by status, date ranges, and search by order code.

The operation returns order summaries optimized for list display, including order code, total price, status, and item count. Full order details with items and shipments are available through the GET /orders/{orderId} endpoint.

Authentication required: Only the authenticated customer's orders are returned. Administrators have separate oversight endpoints for viewing all platform orders.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_orders table filtered by the authenticated member's member_id. Apply pagination using cursor-based or offset-based approach. Support filtering by: status (exact match or array), created_at date range (gte/lte), order code search (partial match). Support sorting by created_at (asc/desc), total_price (asc/desc). Default sort: created_at DESC. Join with shopping_mall_order_items to compute item count per order. Exclude soft-deleted orders (deleted_at IS NULL). Return IPageIShoppingMallOrder.ISummary with pagination metadata (page, limit, total count, hasMore). Handle empty result sets gracefully. Validate date range formats. Reject invalid status values.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of order summary records for the authenticated customer, including pagination metadata for navigation.

requestBody.description: Search criteria including status filters, order code search, date range filters, pagination parameters (page, limit), and sorting options (field, direction).

operations.description:
Retrieves the complete details of a specific order including order items, product snapshots, and shipment tracking information.

This endpoint returns a single order with all its constituent data: order metadata (code, total price, timestamps), the list of order items with product details and variant options, associated shipments with carrier and tracking information, and the shipping address used for the order.

Customers can only access their own orders. The order items include snapshot data preserving the product name, description, variant price, and seller shop information at the time of purchase. Each shipment shows tracking number, carrier name, and delivery status.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_orders table by UUID primary key. Verify the authenticated customer's member_id matches the order's member_id for authorization. Eager load related shopping_mall_order_items with their shopping_mall_order_item_snapshots and shopping_mall_order_item_snapshot_options. Include shopping_mall_shipments with carrier and tracking details. Join with shopping_mall_customer_addresses to include the shipping address snapshot if available. Return 404 if order not found or access denied. Do not include soft-deleted orders unless explicitly requested for admin oversight.

operations.description:
Place a new order by processing the customer's shopping cart items into a permanent order record.

This endpoint creates a complete order transaction, capturing all cart items with their product details, prices, and quantities at the time of purchase. The system generates a unique order code for customer reference and calculates the total order value. Each order item is linked to its product, variant, and seller for fulfillment tracking.

Upon successful order creation, the customer's cart items are removed, inventory records are created to deduct stock quantities, and the order enters the 'paid' status awaiting seller shipment. The operation is atomic - if any step fails (payment, inventory deduction, order item creation), the entire transaction is rolled back.

The returned order object includes all order items with their initial 'paid' status. Shipments are created later by sellers when they fulfill the order items.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new order for the authenticated customer through the following steps:

1. Validate the customer's cart exists and contains at least one item
2. Retrieve all cart items with their associated product variants
3. Validate all variants are available (not deleted, have sufficient stock)
4. Calculate total price from cart items (quantity × variant price or product base price)
5. Generate unique order code (format: date-based + sequence)
6. Create shopping_mall_orders record with member_id, code, total_price, timestamps
7. For each cart item, create shopping_mall_order_items record with:
   - shopping_mall_order_id (new order)
   - shopping_mall_product_id
   - shopping_mall_product_variant_id
   - shopping_mall_seller_id (from variant's product)
   - quantity, price (snapshot at purchase time)
   - status: 'paid'
   - timestamps
8. Create inventory records for each variant to deduct stock quantities
9. Remove all cart items from the customer's cart
10. Return the complete order object with all order items

Use database transaction to ensure atomicity. If any step fails, rollback entire operation. Return appropriate error responses for insufficient stock, deleted variants, or payment failures.

responseBody.description: Complete order object including all order items with their initial 'paid' status, order code for customer reference, and total price snapshot.

requestBody.description: Order creation request containing shipping address reference and optional payment method information. The cart items are automatically converted to order items - no need to specify them explicitly as they come from the customer's active cart.

Retrieve the snapshot of a specific order item showing the product name, description, variant price, and seller profile information as they appeared at the time of purchase.

This endpoint provides read-only access to the immutable order item snapshot, which preserves the exact state of the product and seller profile when the order was placed. This ensures accurate order history even if the original product has been modified or deleted, or if the seller has changed their shop name or logo.

Customers can access snapshots for their own order items through their order history. Sellers can view snapshots for order items containing their products. Administrators can view any order item snapshot on the platform for dispute resolution and oversight purposes.

The snapshot includes the product name, product description, variant price paid, seller shop name, and seller logo URL as they existed at purchase time. This endpoint is essential for customer order history viewing, seller order fulfillment reference, and administrative dispute resolution.

Query the shopping_mall_order_item_snapshots table by joining with shopping_mall_order_items to verify the orderId matches the orderItemId.

Then retrieve the snapshot from shopping_mall_order_item_snapshots where shopping_mall_order_item_id = orderItemId.

Apply authorization checks:
- Customer (member): Verify the order's member_id matches the authenticated customer's ID
- Seller: Verify the order item's shopping_mall_seller_id matches the authenticated seller's ID
- Admin/Super Admin: Allow access to any snapshot

Return the full snapshot record including product_name, product_description, variant_price, seller_shop_name, seller_logo_url, and created_at.

If no snapshot exists for the order item (should not happen in normal operation), return 404.

The options are immutable historical records preserved in the order item snapshot. They remain accessible even if the original product or variant has been modified or deleted, ensuring accurate order history for customers and dispute resolution support for administrators.

Return options as an array of key-value pair objects. Apply authorization checks: customers can only access their own orders, sellers can access order items with their products, administrators have full access.

operations.description:
Create a new shipment for order items.

Sellers can create shipments for their order items that have paid status. A shipment can contain one or more order items from the same seller only. Different sellers always ship separately, resulting in different shipments. Sellers can choose to ship items individually by creating separate shipments for each item, or bundle multiple items together into a single shipment.

When creating a shipment, sellers must provide tracking information including the carrier name and tracking number. All items included in the same shipment share the same tracking information. When a shipment is created, all order items included in that shipment automatically change to shipped status.

The seller identity is determined from the authentication context. Only order items belonging to the authenticated seller can be included in the shipment.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new shipment record in shopping_mall_shipments table.

1. Validate the order exists and belongs to a customer (member_id reference).
2. Verify the authenticated seller has order items in this order with paid status.
3. Validate all provided order item IDs belong to the authenticated seller.
4. Validate all order items have status 'paid' (not already shipped, cancelled, or refunded).
5. Validate order items are not already assigned to another shipment (shopping_mall_shipment_id is null).
6. Create shipment record with: shopping_mall_order_id, shopping_mall_seller_id (from auth), carrier_name, tracking_number, shipped_at (current timestamp).
7. Update all included order items: set shopping_mall_shipment_id to new shipment ID, set status to 'shipped'.
8. Return the created shipment entity.

Error cases:
- Order not found → 404
- Order items not found or don't belong to seller → 404
- Order items already shipped/assigned to shipment → 400
- Order items not in paid status → 400
- Mixed sellers in order item list → 400

responseBody.description: The created shipment entity with tracking information and timestamps.

The response includes shipment summary information such as carrier name, tracking number, shipping timestamp, delivery status, and the count of order items in each shipment. Results are sorted by shipping date in descending order (newest first) and support pagination for efficient browsing of large shipment histories.

Only shipments belonging to the authenticated seller are returned. Soft-deleted shipments are automatically excluded from results.

This endpoint returns complete shipment details including carrier name, tracking number, shipping timestamp, and delivery confirmation status. Sellers can use this to view tracking information for shipments they have created and monitor delivery progress.

The shipment must belong to the authenticated seller. Authorization middleware validates that the seller can only access shipments they created. If the shipment belongs to a different seller or does not exist, the request will be rejected.

The response includes all shipment metadata: carrier information for customer tracking, shipped_at timestamp marking when items transitioned to shipped status, and delivered_at timestamp (if delivery has been confirmed either manually by customer or automatically after 14 days).

operations.description:
Update shipment tracking information.

This endpoint allows sellers to modify the tracking information for a shipment they created. Sellers can update the carrier name and/or tracking number if they need to correct mistakes or if the carrier information changes before delivery.

Tracking information can only be updated while the shipment has not been delivered. Once the delivered_at timestamp is set (either by customer confirmation or automatic delivery after 14 days), the tracking information becomes immutable and cannot be modified.

This endpoint is restricted to the seller who owns the shipment. Other sellers and unauthorized users cannot access or modify shipments they do not own.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update the shopping_mall_shipments record by shipmentId.

Implementation steps:
1. Validate the authenticated user is a seller
2. Query the shipment by id, ensuring shopping_mall_seller_id matches the authenticated seller's id
3. Validate the shipment exists and has not been delivered (delivered_at is null)
4. Allow updating carrier_name and/or tracking_number from the request body
5. Validate carrier_name and tracking_number are non-empty strings (1-255 characters)
6. Do not allow modifying shipped_at, shopping_mall_order_id, shopping_mall_seller_id, or delivered_at
7. Update the record and return the full shipment object

Edge cases:
- Return 404 if shipment not found or seller doesn't own it
- Return 400 if shipment already delivered (delivered_at is not null)
- Return 400 if carrier_name or tracking_number is empty or missing
- Return 403 if authenticated user is not a seller

The shipped_at timestamp remains unchanged (set at creation time). The delivered_at field is controlled by customer delivery confirmation or automatic delivery, not by seller update.

This endpoint retrieves cancellation requests based on search criteria provided in the request body. The results are filtered according to the caller's role and permissions: customers can only view their own cancellation requests, sellers can view cancellation requests for order items from their products, and administrators can view all cancellation requests across the platform.

The search supports filtering by cancellation status (pending, approved, rejected), date ranges for creation and response timestamps, and specific order item references. Results are paginated using cursor-based pagination for efficient handling of large result sets, with sorting options by creation date, response date, or status.

Each cancellation request in the response includes the request ID, order item reference, customer information, cancellation reason, current status, and timestamps. For seller and administrator views, additional context such as product and order details may be included.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:

Apply role-based data isolation:
- member (customer): Filter by shopping_mall_member_id = current user's ID
- seller: Join with shopping_mall_order_items on order_item_id, filter by shopping_mall_seller_id = current seller's ID
- admin/superAdmin: No filtering, can access all records

Support search filters:
- status: Filter by cancellation status (pending, approved, rejected)
- orderItemId: Filter by specific order item ID
- createdAt: Date range filter for request creation
- respondedAt: Date range filter for seller response

Join with shopping_mall_order_items to get order context.
Join with shopping_mall_members for customer information.
Apply cursor-based pagination using created_at timestamp.
Sort by created_at DESC by default (newest first).

Handle soft-deleted records: Exclude records where deleted_at is not null unless explicitly requested by administrators.

operations.description:
Create a new cancellation request for an order item.

This endpoint allows customers to request cancellation of a specific order item before it has been shipped. The cancellation request enters a pending status awaiting seller review. Customers must provide a reason explaining why they want to cancel the item.

The order item must have a 'paid' status to be eligible for cancellation. Items that have already been shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded cannot be cancelled. Each order item can have at most one cancellation request due to the unique constraint on the order item reference.

Upon successful creation, the cancellation request is associated with the authenticated customer and the specified order item. The seller of the order item will be notified to review and approve or reject the request.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new cancellation request record in the shopping_mall_cancellation_requests table.

1. Validate the authenticated customer (member) exists and is active.
2. Verify the order item exists and belongs to the authenticated customer's order.
3. Check order item status is 'paid' - reject if status is shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded.
4. Verify no existing cancellation request exists for this order item (unique constraint).
5. Validate reason is provided and not empty.
6. Create the cancellation request with:
   - shopping_mall_order_item_id: from request body
   - shopping_mall_member_id: from authenticated session
   - reason: from request body
   - status: 'pending'
   - responded_at: null
   - created_at: current timestamp
   - updated_at: current timestamp
7. Return the created cancellation request entity.

Error handling:
- 404 if order item not found
- 400 if order item status is not 'paid'
- 409 if cancellation request already exists for this order item
- 400 if reason is missing or empty

requestBody.description: Cancellation request creation data including the order item to cancel and the customer's reason for cancellation.

Snapshots are immutable audit records that preserve the complete history including status changes, customer's cancellation reason, seller's response reason (if rejected), and review timestamps. This endpoint supports dispute resolution by allowing customers, sellers, and administrators to review the full progression of the cancellation request.

The response is paginated to handle cases where many state changes occurred. Results are sorted by created_at in ascending order to show the historical timeline from initial request to current state.

Retrieve a paginated list of refund requests with filtering and search capabilities.

This endpoint provides customers and administrators with the ability to browse refund requests. Customers see only their own refund requests, while administrators can view all refund requests across the platform for oversight and management purposes.

**Search and Filtering**

Supports filtering by refund status (pending, approved, rejected) to find requests in specific workflow states. Date range filters allow searching by creation date to locate requests from specific time periods. Additional filters may include order item references or product searches.

**Response Data**

Returns summary information for each refund request including the request ID, current status, customer reason, associated order item details, product information, and timestamps. Full refund request details can be retrieved via the GET /refund-requests/{refundRequestId} endpoint.

**Authorization**

Members can only access their own refund requests. Administrators and super administrators have platform-wide visibility to all refund requests for oversight and intervention purposes.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_refund_requests table with pagination and filtering. Apply status filter (pending/approved/rejected), date range filters on created_at. For member actors, filter by shopping_mall_member_id to show only their own requests. For admin/superAdmin actors, return all requests platform-wide. Join with shopping_mall_order_items to include product name, variant details, and order information. Join with shopping_mall_products for product thumbnail. Return cursor-based pagination with summary fields including id, status, reason, order item details, product info, and timestamps. Sort by created_at descending by default (newest first).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of refund request summary records with status, reason, order item details, and product information.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for filtering refund requests including status, date ranges, and pagination parameters.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific refund request by its unique identifier.

This operation returns the complete details of a refund request including the customer's reason, current review status, and timestamps. The refund request contains information about which order item is being refunded and which customer submitted the request.

Access is restricted to the customer who submitted the refund request and the seller who owns the order item. Administrators can also access any refund request for oversight purposes.

The response includes all refund request fields: member ID, order item ID, reason text, status (pending/approved/rejected), review timestamp, and audit timestamps.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_refund_requests table by primary key UUID.

Validate the refundRequestId parameter is a valid UUID format.
Retrieve the refund request record including all fields: shopping_mall_member_id, shopping_mall_order_item_id, reason, status, reviewed_at, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at.

Authorization check: Verify the requesting user is either (1) the customer who submitted the refund request (matching shopping_mall_member_id), (2) the seller who owns the order item (join with shopping_mall_order_items to get shopping_mall_seller_id), or (3) an administrator with oversight permissions.

If refund request not found or user lacks permission, return 404.
If refund request is soft-deleted (deleted_at is not null), return 404.

Return the full IShoppingMallRefundRequest entity with all fields populated.

responseBody.description: Complete refund request record including customer reason, review status, and all audit timestamps.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the refund request to retrieve (UUID format).
parameters.name: refundRequestId

operations.description:
Create a refund request for a delivered order item.

Customers can request a refund for individual order items that have been delivered. The refund request must be submitted within 7 days of the item's delivery date. Each order item can have only one refund request.

The request requires the order item ID and a reason text explaining why the customer wants a refund. The reason is mandatory and must be provided at submission time.

The system validates that the order item has 'delivered' status, belongs to the requesting customer, and is within the 7-day refund window. If any validation fails, the request is rejected with an appropriate error response.

Upon successful creation, the refund request enters 'pending' status awaiting seller review. The seller can then approve or reject the request through separate endpoints.
operations.name: create
operations.specification: Create a refund request for a delivered order item. Validate that the order item exists and has 'delivered' status. Verify the order item belongs to the requesting customer (member). Check that the refund request is within 7 days of the item's delivery date. Ensure the reason field is not empty. Verify no existing refund request exists for this order item (unique constraint on shopping_mall_order_item_id). Create the refund request record with status 'pending'. Return the created refund request entity. If validation fails at any step, return appropriate error response.

responseBody.description: The created refund request entity with pending status, including the order item reference, reason, and timestamps.

requestBody.description: Refund request creation data including the order item ID and customer's reason for the refund.

prerequisites.description: Order must be created first to establish the order items that can be refunded. The refund request references an order_item_id which is created as part of the order placement process.

operations.description:
Retrieve the complete history of state changes for a specific refund request.

This endpoint returns all snapshots associated with a refund request, ordered chronologically by creation timestamp. Each snapshot captures the refund request status, customer reason, and seller response details at a specific moment in time, providing an immutable audit trail for dispute resolution.

Snapshots are created automatically whenever the refund request status changes or when the seller responds to the request. The snapshot chain preserves the full lifecycle from initial submission through final resolution, including all intermediate states.

Results are paginated and support filtering by status and date range. The snapshots are ordered by created_at in ascending order to show the progression of state changes from oldest to newest.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_refund_request_snapshots table filtered by shopping_mall_refund_request_id parameter.

Apply pagination with cursor-based or offset-based pagination. Support filtering by status field (pending, approved, rejected) and created_at date range.

Order results by created_at ascending to show chronological progression of state changes.

Join with shopping_mall_refund_requests to verify the refund request exists and caller has permission to access it.

Return IPageIShoppingMallRefundRequestSnapshot.ISummary with snapshot summary fields: id, status, reason, seller_response_type, seller_response_comment, created_at.

Handle edge cases: refund request not found (404), no snapshots exist (return empty page), caller lacks permission (403).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of refund request snapshot summary records showing the complete history of state changes for the refund request.

parameters.description: UUID of the refund request to retrieve snapshots for (scoped to the refund request).
parameters.name: refundRequestId

requestBody.description: Search criteria including status filter, created_at date range, and pagination parameters (page, limit, sort).

prerequisites.description: Refund request must be created before its snapshot history can be retrieved

operations.description:
Search and list post-purchase cancellation requests with pagination and filtering capabilities.

This endpoint retrieves cancellation requests based on the caller's role and permissions. Customers can view their own cancellation requests, sellers can view requests for order items belonging to their products, and administrators can view all cancellation requests across the platform.

The operation supports filtering by cancellation status (pending, approved, rejected), date ranges for request creation, and pagination parameters for efficient browsing of large result sets. Results are sorted by creation date in descending order (newest first) by default.

Each cancellation request record includes the customer's reason, current status, seller response (if any), and timestamps. The response uses summary DTOs optimized for list displays, excluding detailed snapshot history which can be retrieved via the dedicated snapshot endpoint.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the shopping_mall_post_purchase_cancellation_requests table with role-based data isolation.

For member (customer) actors: Filter by shopping_mall_member_id matching the authenticated user's ID.
For seller actors: Filter by shopping_mall_seller_id matching the authenticated seller's ID.
For admin/superAdmin actors: No filtering, return all records.

Apply search filters from request body:
- status: exact match filter (pending, approved, or rejected)
- createdAtFrom: filter created_at >= value
- createdAtTo: filter created_at <= value
- orderId: filter by associated order (requires join with shopping_mall_order_items)

Implement cursor-based pagination using created_at and id for consistent ordering.
Sort by created_at DESC, then by id DESC for deterministic ordering.

Join with shopping_mall_order_items to include order information in summary.
Join with shopping_mall_members for customer display name.
Join with shopping_mall_products (through order item) for product name in summary.

Handle soft-delete: Exclude records where deleted_at is not null unless actor is admin.

Return IPageIShoppingMallPostPurchaseCancellationRequest.ISummary with pagination metadata.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of cancellation request summary records with customer, seller, order item, and product information optimized for administrative and user-facing list displays.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for filtering cancellation requests including status filter, creation date range, order ID filter, and pagination parameters (take, skip, orderBy).

This endpoint returns the complete cancellation request record including the customer's cancellation reason, current workflow status (pending, approved, or rejected), and the seller's response reason if the request was rejected. Customers can use this to check the status of their cancellation requests. Sellers can access requests for order items belonging to their products. Administrators can view all cancellation requests for oversight purposes.

The cancellation request is linked to a specific order item and can only be created for items with 'paid' status before shipment. Each order item can have at most one cancellation request.

3. Apply authorization checks: allow access if the caller is the requesting customer (member), the reviewing seller, or an administrator.
4. Return the full cancellation request entity.
5. Handle not found: return 404 if no cancellation request exists with the given ID.
6. Handle unauthorized: return 403 if the caller is not authorized to view this cancellation request.

8. Return the created cancellation request entity

- 400 if order item status is not 'paid'

operations.description:
Create a refund request for a delivered order item.

Customers can request a refund for individual order items that have been delivered. The request must be submitted within 7 days of the delivery date and includes a required reason explaining the refund request. Each order item can have at most one refund request.

The refund request enters a pending status awaiting seller review. Sellers can approve or reject the request through their dashboard. Upon approval, the system initiates the refund process and restores inventory stock.

operations.specification:
Create a new refund request record in shopping_mall_refund_requests table.

Validation requirements:
1. Verify the order item exists and has 'delivered' status
2. Check that no existing refund request exists for this order item (unique constraint on shopping_mall_order_item_id)
3. Validate the request is within 7 days of the order item's delivery timestamp
4. Ensure reason text is provided and not empty
5. Verify the authenticated member is the customer who placed the order

Implementation steps:
1. Query shopping_mall_order_items by provided orderItemId
2. Validate order item status is 'delivered'
3. Check created_at + 7 days >= current timestamp for delivery window
4. Query existing refund requests for this order item (should be none)
5. Create refund request with status='pending', member_id from session, provided orderItemId and reason
6. Return the created refund request entity

Error handling:
- 400: Order item not in 'delivered' status
- 400: Refund request outside 7-day window
- 400: Empty or missing reason
- 409: Refund request already exists for this order item
- 403: Authenticated user is not the order owner

operations.description:
Search and list customer reviews with pagination and filtering capabilities.

This endpoint retrieves reviews from the system with support for multiple filter criteria. It is commonly used to display reviews on product detail pages (filtered by product_id) or to show a customer's review history (filtered by member_id). Results are sorted by creation date in descending order (newest first) to show recent feedback prominently.

The endpoint supports filtering by product to show all reviews for a specific product, by member to show a customer's review history, by rating range to find reviews within specific satisfaction levels, and by date range to find reviews from specific time periods. Pagination is applied to all results to handle large datasets efficiently.

Only non-deleted reviews are returned in the results. Deleted reviews are excluded from the response but their snapshots remain preserved in the system for audit purposes.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_reviews table with pagination and filtering.

Apply filters:
- shopping_mall_product_id: filter by specific product (for product detail pages)
- shopping_mall_member_id: filter by specific customer (for profile pages)
- rating: filter by rating range (min/max)
- created_at: filter by date range (from/to)

Exclude soft-deleted reviews (deleted_at IS NOT NULL).
Sort by created_at DESC (newest first).
Apply cursor-based or offset pagination based on request parameters.

Join with shopping_mall_members to include customer display name in summary.
Join with shopping_mall_products to include product name in summary if needed.

Return IPageIShoppingMallReview.ISummary with pagination metadata.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of review summary records sorted by newest first, optimized for display on product detail pages and customer profile pages.

requestBody.description: Search criteria including product ID filter, member ID filter, rating range, date range, and pagination parameters for browsing reviews.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single review by its unique identifier.

This endpoint returns the complete review record including the star rating, optional text content, and metadata such as creation and update timestamps. The review is identified by its UUID and includes references to the customer who wrote it, the product being reviewed, and the associated order.

Deleted reviews (with deleted_at set) are not accessible through this endpoint to maintain data consistency with public display behavior. Only reviews in active state can be retrieved.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the shopping_mall_reviews table by the provided reviewId UUID parameter.

Retrieve the full review record including all fields: id, shopping_mall_member_id, shopping_mall_product_id, shopping_mall_order_id, shopping_mall_order_item_id, rating, content, created_at, updated_at.

Exclude reviews where deleted_at is not null - these soft-deleted reviews should return 404 Not Found.

Join with shopping_mall_members to include customer display name if needed for response enrichment.

Join with shopping_mall_products to include product name for context.

Return 404 if review not found or if review is soft-deleted.

Ensure the authenticated user has permission to view this review (public for product page display, or owner-only for management operations).

responseBody.description: Complete review record including rating, optional content, and timestamps for a single review entity.

parameters.description: UUID identifier of the review to retrieve.
parameters.name: reviewId

operations.description:
Create a new product review for a delivered order item.

This operation allows customers to submit reviews for products they have purchased and received. A review can only be created after the order item status is 'delivered', ensuring customers have actually received the product before providing feedback.

Each review requires a mandatory star rating from 1 to 5 stars. The text content is optional, allowing customers to leave rating-only reviews or provide detailed written feedback. The system enforces one review per order item through a unique constraint on the order item reference.

Reviews are associated with the customer account, product, order, and specific order item. This linkage enables verification of purchase history and delivery status before allowing review creation. Once created, reviews are displayed on the product detail page sorted by newest first.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new review record in shopping_mall_reviews table.

1. Validate request body: rating must be integer 1-5, content is optional string
2. Verify the authenticated customer owns the order_item by joining order_items -> orders -> member_id
3. Verify the order_item status is 'delivered' before allowing review creation
4. Check unique constraint on shopping_mall_order_item_id - reject if review already exists for this order item
5. Insert review with: id (UUID), shopping_mall_member_id (from session), shopping_mall_product_id, shopping_mall_order_id, shopping_mall_order_item_id, rating, content (nullable), created_at, updated_at
6. Return the created review entity with all fields
7. Handle unique constraint violation with 409 Conflict if review already exists for order item
8. Handle delivery status check failure with 403 Forbidden if order item not delivered

responseBody.description: The created review entity with all fields including generated timestamps and references.

requestBody.description: Review creation data including the product, order, order item references, mandatory star rating, and optional text content.

prerequisites.description: Order must be created with order items before a review can be submitted. The order_item referenced in the review must exist and have 'delivered' status, which requires the order to be placed first and fulfilled through shipment and delivery.

operations.description:
Update an existing review's rating and/or text content.

This endpoint allows customers to modify their own reviews after submission. Customers can update the star rating (1-5 stars) and/or the optional text content. The review must exist and not be deleted.

Only the customer who created the review can edit it. If a customer attempts to edit another customer's review, the request is rejected with a 403 Forbidden error. If the review does not exist or has been deleted, the request is rejected with a 404 Not Found error.

Every review edit automatically creates a review snapshot that preserves the previous state including the rating and text content before the change. This ensures a complete history of all changes is maintained for dispute resolution. Snapshots are immutable and cannot be deleted.

The rating must be between 1 and 5 stars inclusive. The content field is optional and can be updated to any text value or set to null to remove the text content while keeping the rating.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update the review identified by reviewId with the provided rating and/or content.

1. Validate reviewId format (UUID)
2. Query shopping_mall_reviews table for the review with matching id
3. Verify review exists and deleted_at is null (not soft deleted)
4. Verify ownership: check that shopping_mall_member_id matches the authenticated customer's ID
5. If ownership check fails, return 403 Forbidden
6. Validate rating: must be integer between 1 and 5 inclusive
7. Validate content: can be string or null
8. Create a review snapshot before updating: insert into shopping_mall_review_snapshots with current review state (rating, content, timestamps)
9. Update the review record with new rating and/or content
10. Update updated_at timestamp to current time
11. Return the updated review object with all fields

Edge cases:
- Review not found: return 404
- Review is soft deleted: return 404
- Not the review owner: return 403
- Rating outside 1-5 range: return 400 Bad Request
- Concurrent edit: use optimistic locking if implemented

responseBody.description: The updated review object with the new rating and/or content values.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the review to update (UUID format).
parameters.name: reviewId

requestBody.description: Update payload containing the new rating and/or text content for the review.

operations.description:
Delete a customer's own review from the system.

This operation allows customers to delete reviews they have written. When a review is deleted, it is soft-deleted by setting the deleted_at timestamp, which removes it from public view on product detail pages and excludes it from average rating calculations. The review content is no longer accessible through normal queries but remains in the database for audit purposes.

Review snapshots created during previous edits are preserved and cannot be deleted, maintaining a complete historical audit trail. Only the customer who created the review can delete it - attempts to delete another customer's review are rejected with a permission error.

After deletion, the product's average rating is recalculated excluding this review. If no non-deleted reviews remain for the product, no average rating is displayed.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Authenticate the requesting customer and extract their member ID from the session.

2. Query the shopping_mall_reviews table to find the review by the provided reviewId.

3. If review not found, return 404 Not Found error.

4. Validate ownership: compare the review's shopping_mall_member_id with the authenticated customer's member ID. If they don't match, return 403 Forbidden error (customer can only delete their own reviews).

5. Check if review is already deleted (deleted_at is not null). If already deleted, return 404 Not Found (treat as non-existent).

6. Perform soft deletion: update the review's deleted_at field to the current timestamp.

7. Create a review snapshot before deletion to preserve the final state (rating, content, timestamps) for audit trail. Insert into shopping_mall_review_snapshots table.

8. Return 204 No Content response (successful deletion with no response body).

Edge cases:
- Review not found: 404
- Not the review owner: 403 Forbidden
- Already deleted review: 404
- Database transaction failure: rollback and return 500 Internal Server Error

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the review to delete (UUID format).
parameters.name: reviewId

prerequisites.description: Review must be created before it can be deleted - establishes the review entity with member ownership that the delete operation validates

operations.description:
Retrieve paginated list of historical snapshots for a specific review.

This endpoint returns all snapshots created when the review was edited, preserving the rating and content values at each edit point. Snapshots are ordered by creation timestamp (newest first) to show the most recent edit history prominently.

Review snapshots are immutable audit records automatically created by the system whenever a customer edits their review. Each snapshot captures the exact state before the edit was applied, enabling dispute resolution and audit trail reconstruction.

Access is restricted to the review owner, administrators, and sellers who own the product being reviewed. Unauthorized access attempts are rejected with access denied errors.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_review_snapshots table filtered by shopping_mall_review_id matching the path parameter.

Apply pagination using cursor-based or offset-based approach with limit and offset from request body.

Order results by created_at DESC to show newest snapshots first.

Enforce access control: allow only review owner (customer who created the review), administrators (any grade), or seller who owns the product associated with the review.

Join with shopping_mall_reviews to verify ownership and product association.

Return IPageIShoppingMallReviewSnapshot.ISummary with snapshot summaries including id, rating, content preview, and created_at timestamp.

Handle edge case: return empty array if review has no snapshots (never edited).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of review snapshot summaries showing the edit history timeline.

parameters.description: UUID of the parent review to retrieve snapshots for (scoped to specific review).

requestBody.description: Search criteria including pagination parameters (page, limit) and optional sorting options for review snapshot history.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific review snapshot by its ID within the context of a parent review.

Review snapshots are immutable audit records automatically created whenever a customer edits their review. Each snapshot preserves the exact rating and content values at the moment of edit, enabling historical tracking of review changes for dispute resolution and administrative oversight.

This endpoint returns the complete snapshot record including the star rating, optional text content, and creation timestamp. The snapshot cannot be modified or deleted, ensuring a permanent audit trail.

Access to review snapshots is restricted for privacy and security. Only the customer who owns the parent review can view its snapshots, or administrators with oversight privileges. If the parent review has been soft-deleted, only administrators can access the snapshots. Customers attempting to access another customer's review snapshots will receive an access denied error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_review_snapshots table by snapshot ID with review ID validation.

Implementation steps:
1. Validate snapshotId exists in shopping_mall_review_snapshots table

3. Check authorization: requesting user must be either (a) the owner of the parent review (shopping_mall_member_id matches authenticated user) or (b) an administrator
4. If review is soft-deleted (deleted_at is not null), only administrators can access snapshots
5. Return full snapshot record including id, rating, content, created_at

Edge cases:
- Snapshot not found: return 404
- ReviewId mismatch: return 404 (do not reveal snapshot exists under different review)
- Unauthorized access: return 403
- Review owner accessing their own deleted review's snapshots: allowed
- Customer accessing another customer's review snapshots: rejected with 403

responseBody.description: Complete review snapshot record preserving historical review state at the time of edit.

operations.description:
Retrieves the seller's dashboard summary with key statistics about their shop performance.

Returns aggregated metrics including total product count, total order item count, pending cancellation request count, and pending refund request count. This endpoint provides sellers with a quick overview of their shop status upon login or dashboard access.

The dashboard data is scoped to the authenticated seller's account only. Sellers can view these statistics to monitor their business activity and pending customer requests requiring attention.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the authenticated seller's dashboard statistics:

1. Count products from shopping_mall_products table where seller_id matches authenticated seller
2. Count order items from shopping_mall_order_items table where seller_id matches authenticated seller
3. Count pending cancellation requests from shopping_mall_cancellation_requests table where seller_id matches and status is 'pending'
4. Count pending refund requests from shopping_mall_refund_requests table where seller_id matches and status is 'pending'

Return aggregated dashboard summary object. No pagination needed as this returns single summary record. Ensure seller is authenticated and has approved seller status before returning data.

responseBody.description: Seller dashboard summary containing aggregated statistics about products, orders, and pending requests.

operations.description:
Retrieves dashboard summary statistics for administrator promotion requests.

This endpoint provides super administrators with an overview of the promotion request workflow, including counts of requests by status. The dashboard helps super administrators understand the volume of pending requests awaiting review and track overall promotion request activity.

The response includes total request counts, pending requests awaiting review, approved requests where applicants were promoted to administrator, and rejected requests. This data enables super administrators to prioritize their review workload and monitor the promotion pipeline.
operations.name: dashboard
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_admin_promotion_requests table and aggregate counts by status. Count total requests, pending requests (status='pending'), approved requests (status='approved'), and rejected requests (status='rejected'). Filter to exclude soft-deleted records (deleted_at IS NULL). Return aggregated statistics as dashboard summary object. Only accessible to super administrators - verify caller has grade='super' in shopping_mall_administrators table.

responseBody.description: Dashboard summary containing aggregated counts of administrator promotion requests by status.

operations.description:
Retrieve the authenticated user's own administrator promotion request.

This endpoint allows members and sellers to view their submitted administrator promotion request, including the current status (pending, approved, or rejected), the reason they provided, and any rejection notes from the super administrator reviewer.

Users can only have one pending promotion request at a time. If a previous request was rejected, they may submit a new request. Approved requests indicate the user has been promoted to regular administrator status.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_admin_promotion_requests table filtered by the authenticated user's ID.

For member users: Join with shopping_mall_admin_promotion_request_of_members on shopping_mall_member_id = authenticated_user_id.
For seller users: Join with shopping_mall_admin_promotion_request_of_sellers on shopping_mall_seller_id = authenticated_user_id.

Return the promotion request record if found, including: id, actor_type, reason, status, rejection_note, reviewed_by_super_admin_id, created_at, updated_at.

Return null if the user has never submitted a promotion request.

Exclude soft-deleted records (deleted_at IS NOT NULL).

No pagination needed as each user can have only one active request at a time per business rules.

responseBody.description: The user's administrator promotion request details, or null if no request has been submitted.

operations.description:

This endpoint allows members and sellers to view their submitted administrator promotion request, including the current status (pending, approved, or rejected), the reason they provided, and any rejection notes from the super administrator reviewer.
